record.original_question: Find a fast algorithm for determining the diameter of a graph, improving on the matrix-multiplication-based O(n^2.496) upper bound cited in the source and the O(n log n) lower bound mentioned there.

evidence.quote: Find a fast algorithm to determine the diameter of a graph. Using matrix multiplication one can determine the diameter in time O(n^2.496) [1]. On the other hand, the best known lower bound is O(n log n).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite simple connected graph with $|V|=n$ vertices, where the distance $d(u,v)$ between two vertices $u,v\in V$ is the number of edges in a shortest path connecting them. The diameter of $G$ is defined as
$$\mathrm{diam}(G)=\max_{u,v\in V} d(u,v).$$
Using fast matrix multiplication, $\mathrm{diam}(G)$ can be computed in time $O(n^{2.496})$, while a trivial information-theoretic argument gives a lower bound of $\Omega(n\log n)$.

Design an algorithm that, given $G$ as input, computes $\mathrm{diam}(G)$ exactly in time strictly better than $O(n^{2.496})$, or alternatively prove a stronger (unconditional) lower bound than $\Omega(n\log n)$ on the worst-case time complexity of any such algorithm. Close, as much as possible, the gap between these upper and lower bounds.
artifact.status_search_result: The exact complexity of computing graph diameter remains open. The best exact algorithms for dense unweighted graphs still rely on fast matrix multiplication (currently around O(n^ω) with ω < 2.373). Roditty and Vassilevska Williams established a conditional lower bound: any O((n+m)^(2−ε)) algorithm for diameter would refute the Strong Exponential Time Hypothesis (SETH). However, no unconditional super-(n log n) lower bound is known, and no algorithm beating the matrix-multiplication-based bound is known either, so the gap remains.

status_evidence.title: Fast Approximation Algorithms for the Diameter and Radius of Sparse Graphs (Roditty–Vassilevska Williams)
status_evidence.snippet: An O((n+m)^(2−ε)) algorithm for diameter would refute SETH; exact diameter for dense graphs uses fast matrix multiplication.
status_evidence.claim: No truly subquadratic exact diameter algorithm is known; conditional SETH lower bound matches the matrix-multiplication regime.

status_evidence.title: Towards Tight Approximation Bounds for Graph Diameter and Eccentricities
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses the state of the art on exact and approximate diameter computation and conditional hardness.
status_evidence.claim: Exact diameter complexity remains a central open question with only conditional hardness.
